newsitem.title: UK: HSBC IN BID TO UNSEAT SARACEN FUND MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: HSBC IN BID TO UNSEAT SARACEN FUND MANAGER.

text.p: HSBC Asset Management said on Thursday it wanted to replace SFM Investment Management as the fund manager of the 81 million sterling Saracen Value Trust.
HSBC has approached the board of Saracen and said it had the support of shareholders representing 49.3 percent of Saracen's issued share capital.
Saracen shares were trading at 92 pence, up from 89 at Wednesday's close but a discount to the trust's net asset value (NAV) of 109.82 pence per share.
The directors of Saracen are advising shareholders not to take any action.
This is the latest in a recent string of investment trusts to come under pressure to make changes to enhance shareholder value.
Last week Fleming Far Eastern investment trust proposed to wind its activities down and return cash to shareholders.
And on Thursday investors bid shares of Govett Oriental Investment Trust up to a 52-week high on news that U.S. arbitrageur Sierra Trading had taken a 10 percent holding.

HSBC Asset Management said in a statement it was proposing to waive its management fee for the first two years of any contract and to reduce the notice period from two years to one year at the end of three years.
HSBC also will reduce the management fee to 75 bps from the current 100 bps of total assets less liabilities.
HSBC said if these proposals were not acceptable to Saracen it has the support of shareholders representing 44.3 percent of the issued capital to convene an extraordinary general meeting.
Saracen defended its performance in a statement and said that it has retained Charterhouse Tilney Securities to "explore means of maximising value for shareholders".
In the year to March 1997, Saracen, which invests primarily in small cap shares, achieved a total return of 11.4 percent verses its benchmark index of 15.7 percent.
